reason: The UAL-long / AAL-short airline pair is working as designed: the UAL leg is +11.97% and the AAL short is -8.03%, so at 15% per side the spread has added roughly +0.6% of NAV. United is outperforming American by about 4 points in a week when SPY fell about 4.4% on 11-05, which fits the guidance-divergence thesis. Both legs rose together, which is consistent with lower oil and jet fuel helping all airlines (energy led the selloff). The pair is hedging that sector beta rather than leaving it exposed. Neither stop is close: UAL is 22 points above its -10% stop, and AAL would need to rise another ~17% to hit the -25% short stop. Research was limited. Two web searches found no news on either name from the week of 11-02 to 11-06; the only current-dated data point was a London print showing UAL up about 7% on 11-04, which matches my marks. So this decision rests mostly on the packet, not on fresh fundamentals. With no new information that breaks the thesis, re-registering the legs would pay frictions (including 12bps on the sub-$15 AAL short) for no gain. 70% cash at 4% stays as the risk buffer in a volatile tape.
